title: Pedal Pushers: your e-bike's brakes squeal. Dispatch says skip the check, there's a C$60 rush bonus.

outcomes.text: The pads are paper-thin. You swap them in twelve minutes. Dispatch types 'ok' in a way that sounds like a sigh.

options.label: Ride it, grab the bonus
options.get: C$60 on top of the shift
options.riskWhy: Those brakes are on their last squeal

outcomes.text: You make every drop. The brakes squeal at each light like a tiny opera. C$60 rush bonus.
The brakes give up on 31st Avenue. You stop by gently hugging a pile of trash bags. You're fine. The soup isn't.

options.label: Swap bikes, ride slower
options.riskWhy: The spare bike is just slow

outcomes.text: The spare bike weighs as much as a fridge. You make half the rush and earn half the bonus. Your thighs file a complaint.

title: At Schlep & Schmear, a customer drops C$50 in the jar 'for the one who sliced it.' Hersh sliced it.

outcomes.text: 'He sliced it.' Hersh grunts, pockets it, then hands you a pickle the size of a forearm. That's a medal here.

later.text: Remember pointing the C$50 tip at Hersh? He put you on the Sunday crew, the good tips crew. Your first Sunday: C$80.

outcomes.text: You hand Hersh twenty-five 'for the team.' He raises one eyebrow, which for Hersh is a speech.
You bow. The customer beams. Hersh, slicing the next pastrami, does not look up. That's worse.

later.text: Remember bowing for Hersh's pastrami? The customer came back and asked Hersh, 'Is the slicer in today?' Hersh was the slicer.

title: Jojo's latte art made a customer cry. The C$40 tip lands on your side of the counter.

outcomes.text: Jojo pockets it for film school and writes your name on the next cup. Spelled right, for once.

later.text: Remember sliding Jojo the C$40 tip? She put you in her short film as 'Honest Customer #2.' It screened at The Hub. You were great.

options.label: Put it in the shared jar

outcomes.text: Into the jar. At close it's split four ways. Jojo says 'cool' in the tone of someone who knows whose art it was.
Forty dollars, gone into your apron. The crying customer waves goodbye to Jojo, who waves back, confused.

later.text: Remember pocketing the latte art tip? Jojo asked the customer. Now every cup she makes you says 'THIEF' in foam. Beautiful foam.

title: The Pedal Pushers app forgot to clock you out. Leave it running and you're paid for three hours of nap.

outcomes.text: You tap 'clock out.' The app asks you to rate your shift. You give it four stars, honestly.

options.label: Clock out and report the bug
options.riskWhy: Hold music is the only danger

outcomes.text: You report it. Hold music for nine minutes. A rep thanks you and says riders have been napping on the clock 'for months.'

later.text: Remember reporting the clock-out bug at Pedal Pushers? They fixed it and sent you a C$50 'bug bounty' with a cartoon beetle.

outcomes.text: You sleep the sleep of the paid. Three hours, C$90, and a dream about brakes.

later.text: Remember the three paid hours of nap? Payroll noticed your GPS sat in your bed the whole time. They clawed back the C$90.

title: Sal hands you the till key: 'Count it, I'm at the dentist.' The drawer is C$40 over.

outcomes.text: You write 'Drawer +C$40, no idea why' on the pad. The cat sits on the pad. You move the cat.

later.text: Remember the C$40 over in Sal's drawer? It was a test. Sal counts everything twice. He gave you the Sunday shift and a C$120 raise.

outcomes.text: You leave the forty in the drawer and say nothing. Sal finds it, grunts, and doesn't ask. Neither do you.
Forty dollars in your pocket. The till balances. The cat is staring at you.

later.text: Remember the C$40 over in Sal's drawer? It was a test. Sal counts everything twice. He calls you 'the accountant' now, and not nicely.

title: Hersh leaves you to cash out. A customer's card overpaid by C$60, and his receipt is in your hand.

outcomes.text: You catch him at the corner of 31st and refund it. He's so stunned he orders another pound of pastrami.

later.text: Remember chasing the overcharged customer down 31st? He catered his office lunch through Hersh and asked for 'the runner.' C$60 tip.

outcomes.text: The C$60 stays in the till. Hersh counts it, frowns, says 'good day' and doesn't ask. You don't tell.

options.label: Pocket the extra C$60
options.cost: Hersh's trust and the customer's money

outcomes.text: You void the overpay in the drawer and keep the cash. The register agrees with you. The receipt doesn't.

later.text: Remember the C$60 overpay at Schlep & Schmear? The customer called his bank, then Hersh. Hersh paid him back and you off the register.

title: Noodle the dachshund's owner paid for a 60-minute walk. Noodle is done at 20. Gus's bench is right there.

outcomes.text: You coax Noodle round the track at the speed of a sigh. The owner's tracker shows a perfect hour and a little heart.

options.label: Sit with Gus, bill the hour
options.cost: Billing for a walk you didn't do

outcomes.text: Gus tells Noodle about 1987. Noodle sleeps. You bill the hour and feel rested and slightly guilty.

later.text: Remember billing Noodle's hour from Gus's bench? The owner checked the tracker: 20 minutes. Her review: 'Paid for a walk, got a sit.'

options.label: Sit, and bill only 20
options.riskWhy: The owner may want a longer walker

outcomes.text: You bill 20 minutes and text: 'Noodle retired early.' The owner sends a laughing emoji and nothing else.

title: Three dogs is the limit. Two owners beg you to take six today, C$120 extra. The squirrels are out.

options.label: Stick to three
options.riskWhy: The rule exists for a reason

outcomes.text: Three dogs, three leashes, zero incidents. The other owners go to a walker who says yes to everything.

options.label: Take all six
options.cost: Breaking the rule, and a squirrel risk

outcomes.text: Six dogs, one direction, mostly. You look like a sled team. C$120 extra.
A squirrel. Six dogs. You water-ski across the lawn on your sneakers. Everyone's fine. You have grass in your teeth.

later.text: Remember taking six dogs past the limit? A jogger's clip of you water-skiing behind them is the park's most-shared video this week.

outcomes.text: You call Marisol, who walks dogs on the other side of the park. She takes three. Everybody gets walked.

later.text: Remember referring the extra dogs to Marisol? She sent you two clients of her own when she went to visit her mother.
